new_jobs.title: Senior People Partner
new_jobs.description:
### **About Niantic Spatial**

We are building for the >80% of economic activity that happens beyond the reach of screens. AI has learned from the text, images and video online, but it still lacks an accurate understanding of physical space. That's one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it's the one we're solving at Niantic Spatial.

We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That's why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world's most widely used maps. Now we're building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

### **The Role**

We are looking for a Senior People Partner who combines strong business judgment with hands-on execution. Reporting to the Chief People Officer, you will own People partnership for the business, with a particular focus on engineering and technical teams.

This is a player-coach role on a lean People team. You will coach managers and leaders, strengthen team effectiveness, and personally deliver the work required to turn decisions into action. On any given day, you might help a leader clarify team responsibilities, guide a manager through a performance issue, resolve an employee concern, or use AI to simplify a recurring workflow.

You will independently manage day-to-day People priorities, partnering with the Chief People Officer on broader organizational decisions and particularly complex or sensitive matters. You will also lead defined People programs and projects that support the company’s priorities.

You should understand how engineers work, build credibility with technical leaders, and bring practical experience helping teams perform through ambiguity and change. You are AI-forward in your own work and help others adopt better ways of working.

### **What You’ll Do**

**Partner with leaders to build effective teams**

* Translate business priorities into practical people plans for your groups, including staffing needs, team structure, manager capability, and development.
* Partner with Engineering, Research, Product, and other leaders to understand how their teams operate, identify barriers to execution, and improve effectiveness.
* Help leaders clarify roles, responsibilities, and decision ownership as priorities evolve.
* Surface emerging people and organizational issues early, recommend solutions, and follow through on agreed actions.
* Partner with the Chief People Officer on organizational planning and decisions with broader company implications.

**Coach managers and strengthen accountability**

* Help managers set clear expectations, give direct feedback, address underperformance, and recognize strong contributions.
* Coach managers and leaders on delegation, prioritization, communication, and leading through uncertainty.
* Guide performance reviews, talent discussions, and development planning for your groups, ensuring decisions lead to clear actions and follow-through.
* Help managers maintain a high bar for quality, ownership, collaboration, and speed.
* Build and deliver practical tools and guidance that strengthen everyday management.

**Execute organizational change**

* Help leaders plan and implement team changes, including role clarity, manager preparation, employee communication, and follow-up.
* Support the evolution of working practices as we move from technical exploration toward repeatable customer and business outcomes.
* Identify where unclear ownership, slow decisions, or unnecessary process is limiting progress and work with leaders to address it.
* Use employee feedback and people data to identify patterns, recommend specific actions, and assess progress.

**Own the day-to-day People partnership**

* Serve as a trusted resource for employees and managers, handling sensitive situations with sound judgment, discretion, and care.
* Manage employee relations matters and conduct investigations, partnering with the Chief People Officer and counsel as appropriate.
* Partner with Talent Acquisition and hiring managers on role definition, hiring priorities, candidate assessment, and onboarding.
* Collaborate with Total Rewards on compensation, leveling, promotions, and retention recommendations.
* Own case management, documentation, and follow-through, bringing in additional expertise when needed.
* Contribute to the broader People team by sharing practical approaches and helping colleagues solve problems.

**Improve People programs and use AI to increase effectiveness**

* Lead defined People programs and improvement projects from planning through implementation, coordinating stakeholders and tracking results.
* Use AI tools regularly to accelerate research, analysis, drafting, and workflow improvement, reviewing outputs for accuracy and usefulness and exercising care with sensitive information.
* Identify opportunities to automate repetitive work and create more capacity for manager and employee support.
* Help managers translate changes in AI capabilities into practical development needs and clearer expectations for their teams.
* Use HR systems, people data, and business context to inform recommendations and reduce manual work.
* Build processes that are easy to use and appropriate for our stage.

### **What You Bring**

* Typically eight or more years of progressive People experience, including significant experience as a People Partner or HR Business Partner.
* Direct experience supporting engineering

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager - Incident Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
About GitHub: GitHub is the world’s leading platform for agentic software development — powered by Copilot to build, scale, and deliver secure software. Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.  
Locations: In this role you can work from Remote, United States  
Overview:

GitHub is seeking an experienced and customer-focused Senior Program Manager-Incident Coordinator to independently coordinate complex, high-risk and business-critical customer situations within the Incident Coordination team’s remit.

Senior Program Manager-Incident Coordinator provides leadership during urgent customer-impacting incidents, creating clarity in ambiguous situations, establishing ownership and aligning Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Reliability Engineering, Customer Success and other stakeholders around a clear path forward.

This role requires excellent judgement, composure and the ability to influence without direct authority. The Senior Program Manager-Incident Coordinator must be able to manage several competing workstreams, make explicit prioritization decisions and communicate complex technical situations clearly to customers, senior leaders and technical stakeholders.

The role extends beyond coordinating individual incidents. Senior Program Manager-Incident Coordinators use evidence from incidents and escalations to identify recurring risks, recommend improvements and deliver agreed changes within the incident coordination remit. They partner with accountable teams on broader product, support-process and customer-experience improvements.

Success is measured through effective incident coordination, sound prioritisation, timely and accurate customer communication, reliable handovers and follow-through on agreed actions. The role also contributes to shared improvements that reduce repeat customer impact, avoidable urgent demand and preventable executive escalations.

Responsibilities:

Strategic incident leadership

* Independently lead complex, high-risk customer incidents, prioritising by impact, urgency and risk.

* Create clarity and momentum when cause, ownership, recovery path or customer outcome is uncertain.

* Own coordination, communication, action tracking and handovers across the incident lifecycle.

* Establish clear technical ownership and coordinate workstreams, decisions, risks, dependencies and next steps. Engineering and Support remain accountable for technical decisions, remediation and resource commitments.

* Exercise sound judgement, challenge assumptions and adapt the response as evidence changes.

* Make competing priorities and trade-offs explicit, engaging specialist support or accountable leaders when needed.

new_jobs.description:
**Change Lives With Recovery Innovations!** Our **Mission** is to empower people on their journey to recovery, helping them achieve their goals, rediscover meaning and purpose in life, and reconnect with themselves and their communities. Our **Vision** is to revolutionize healthcare by pioneering innovative solutions that go beyond behavioral health, empowering people to thrive in the communities where they live, work, and play. Join a groundbreaking team at the forefront of **Peer-Powered Support**, empowering individuals on their journey through mental health and substance use challenges! Be part of something bigger—together, we can change lives and create lasting hope!

**Position: Quality & Compliance Operations Coordinator**

**Job Type:** Full-Time; Exempt

**Shift Details:** Monday- Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM

**Work Location:** Remote - Travel required based on business needs

**Salary/Hourly Wage:** $55,000.00 - $65,000.00/annually

**Specialties / Licenses or Certifications:**

**Summary of Job:** The Quality & Compliance Operations Coordinator provides high-reliability administrative, data and workflow infrastructure for the Quality & Compliance department in a multi-state behavioral health organization. The position maintains safety and compliance trackers, performs and quality-checks Project and work management system(s) and related data entry, administers policy and QC support-ticket workflows, maintains CAP/POC and audit trackers, monitors approved automations and recurring tasks, supports regulation-monitoring workflows, prepares reports and meeting materials, maintains audit trails and escalates exceptions. The role is designed for a systems-minded professional who can improve reliability, reduce administrative friction and help qualified reviewers focus on risk and improvement. The position does not independently interpret regulations, make clinical determinations, approve CAPs/POCs, own incident/RCA processes or accept compliance risk.  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

**1. Quality & Compliance Administrative Support:**

* Maintains approved safety, facility, licensing-support, audit, CAP/POC, policy, QC support-ticket, and recurring compliance trackers with accurate owners, due dates, evidence status, and escalation fields.
* Builds accountability into approved systems through named owners, due dates, required evidence, automated reminders, aging, escalation thresholds, dashboards, and visible exception reporting.
* Does not assume responsibility for repeatedly chasing departments or completing work owned by other functions. Maintains visibility, sends system-driven reminders as designed, and escalates overdue or high-risk exceptions to the accountable leader and QC leadership.
* Performs completeness checks, follows up on missing administrative information, and prepares exception lists for qualified QC review.
* Prepares agendas, current trackers, status reports, meeting packets, action logs, and approved QC newsletter materials.

**2. Data, Work Management Platform & Automation Administration:**

* Creates, updates and quality-checks authorized Project and work management system(s) records for policies, QC support tickets, audits, CAPs/POCs, action items, evidence, aging and status.
* Maintains standardized fields, naming conventions, templates, recurring tasks, permissions requests and dashboard source data.
* Maps current-state and future-state QC workflows and identifies non-value added steps, duplicate entry, avoidable handoffs, waiting, rework, and control gaps.
* Partners with Information Technology and the Project Management Office to document requirements, prioritize workflow improvements, test changes, validate automations, support user acceptance testing, and maintain change-control evidence.
* Supports Lean Six Sigma/DMAIC improvement work through process maps, baseline data, cycle-time and defect tracking, action logs, and control-plan administration.
* Performs scheduled health checks of approved reminders, recurring tasks, alerts, dashboards, and integrations.
* Corrects routine configuration or data issues within assigned access; documents automation failures, affected records and administrative impact; and promptly escalates control gaps or system issues.
* Measures whether approved improvements reduce manual effort, duplication, waiting, rework, or data defects and reports results and exceptions to QC leadership.

**3. Compliance & Risk Management:**

* Maintains approved regulatory-source lists and administrative monitoring schedules and routes outputs or potential changes to qualified QC reviewers.

new_jobs.description:
**About Nudge Security**
------------------------

The security perimeter keeps moving. First it was the network, then the endpoint, then identity. Now it’s the AI and SaaS decisions employees make every day: the tools they adopt, the data they connect, and the agents they build. Nudge Security is the workforce security platform for AI, SaaS, and identity, built for this new perimeter.

**Find it. Govern it. Fix it.** We discover every app, account, and AI agent, approved or not. We set guardrails for how they’re used. And where most tools stop at an alert, Nudge works directly with employees to fix the risk without slowing them down.

More than 250 organizations trust Nudge, and over 95% of them stay. Founded in 2021 by Russell Spitler and Jaime Blasco, we’re backed by Ballistic Ventures, Forgepoint Capital, Cerberus Ventures, and Squadra Ventures, and we closed a $22M Series A in November 2025.

**Summary**
-----------

As a Channel Account Manager, you'll help scale Nudge Security's North American partner ecosystem and drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue. This individual contributor role combines strategic planning with hands-on execution across partner recruitment, joint business planning, enablement, and co-selling.

You'll own relationships across a defined territory or partner portfolio, working closely with Sales, Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success. Success requires strong relationships with key cybersecurity partners and the ability to personally equip their sellers to identify opportunities, articulate Nudge Security's value, and move deals forward.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Develop and execute a North American channel plan for your assigned territory or portfolio, with clear partner priorities, pipeline goals, and revenue objectives.
* Build and grow relationships with strategic resellers, solution providers, distributors, MSSPs, and relevant alliance partners; recruit, onboard, and activate new partners where there is a clear business opportunity.
* Create joint business plans, lead quarterly business reviews, and establish mutual accountability for pipeline creation, enablement, and bookings.

* Build practical playbooks and training that help partner sellers recognize customer needs and confidently position Nudge Security. Partner with Sales Engineering for deeper technical enablement and evaluations.
* Collaborate with Marketing on joint campaigns, events, workshops, and demand generation; manage market development funds where applicable and measure resulting pipeline and return on investment.
* Maintain accurate deal registration, forecasting, partner activity, and CRM records, with a consistent operating cadence and clear visibility into partner performance.
* Bring partner feedback and market insights to Sales, Marketing, Product, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success to improve partner execution and the customer experience.
* Represent Nudge Security at partner meetings, executive briefings, industry events, and security conferences.

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

* 7+ years of experience in channel sales, partner management, or alliances, including direct experience at a cybersecurity SaaS company.
* Established, active relationships with key cybersecurity partners such as GuidePoint Security, Optiv, World Wide Technology (WWT), AHEAD, and Trace3, with demonstrated success turning those relationships into pipeline and bookings.
* Ability to provide a professional reference from at least one key channel partner who can speak to your partnership, execution, and business results.
* A proven record of meeting or exceeding channel revenue targets and building repeatable partner-led pipeline within an assigned region or portfolio.
* Strong hands-on partner enablement skills, including the ability to independently deliver sales training and coach partner sellers on messaging, discovery, qualification, and objection handling.
* Experience recruiting and activating partners, developing joint business plans, leading QBRs, and executing co-selling and joint marketing initiatives.
* Ability to learn and clearly communicate Nudge Security's value across AI and SaaS security governance, Shadow AI, and workforce technology risk.
* Strong commercial judgment, executive presence, presentation skills, and relationships across partner leadership and field sales teams.
* A data-driven approach to forecasting, pipeline management, and partner performance, with experience using CRM and partner management tools.
* Comfort building processes and taking ownership in a fast-paced startup environment. Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

### **Why Nudge Security?**

At Nudge Security, you'll have the opportunity to help shape our partner ecosystem and expand how we reach and support customers. You'll work alongside an experienced leadership team, represent a platform addressing AI and SaaS security governance, and have a direct impact on partner growth and company revenue. You'll be part of a collaborative, customer-first culture where your ideas, contributions, and success matter.

### **Compensation + Benefits**

Compensation for this position includes a competitive base salary, uncapped commission, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

Job Summary:

This will require contacting clients, operations personnel, and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) via phone, email, or website.

new_jobs.title: Customer Success Executive
new_jobs.description:
Overview:

HealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market. We're experiencing strong market momentum, with a growing number of health plans choosing HealthEdge to modernize their operations and compete more effectively. As we expand, we're investing in the people who power that growth, making this a pivotal moment to join us and shape the future of healthcare technology. Learn more at HealthEdge.com.

**ROLE SUMMARY**

HealthEdge's customer success strategy depends on four organizational capabilities: achieving customer outcomes, retaining and converting referenceable customers, expanding revenue within the existing customer base, and maintaining data and reporting integrity. The CSE is an essential delivery partner in all four — owning defined workstreams, managing critical relationship layers, and keeping the operational machinery of customer success running with precision.

This is not a support role. It is an outcome ownership role at a defined scope. A CSE at HealthEdge is accountable for the workstreams they own within the customer's success plan — and for keeping those workstreams current, honest, and moving without being asked.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities are organized by the four strategic outcomes the CSE organization exists to deliver. These are not task lists — they are outcome areas with clear accountability.

**Customer Outcomes**

* Own defined workstreams within the Customer Success Plan for every assigned account — keeping your sections current, evidence-based, and tied to the customer's business objectives, not HealthEdge's delivery milestones.
* Support the Senior CSE in quarterbacking execution across Delivery, Operations, Technology, and Product. Own every task you've been assigned until it is closed — not until you've sent it to someone else.
* Understand the HealthEdge platform capabilities relevant to your assigned accounts well enough to support executive preparation and translate delivery activity into customer language.

**Customer Retention &** **Referenceability**

* Surface account risk before the customer does — identify the signal, act on it, and flag it appropriately with context already framed: what you're seeing, why it matters, and what you recommend.
* Own assigned pieces of the Path to Green plan for every at-risk account — keep the issue list current and honest, track every action to closure, and never let a recovery item die in a seam.
* Support reference-development plans by maintaining strong VP/Director relationships that make customers willing, credible advocates.

**Customer Revenue Expansion**

* Maintain a current view of each assigned customer's strategic direction and flag multi-product or cross-sell signals to the Senior CSE with context — what you heard, from whom, and what it might mean commercially.
* Know the basics of each assigned account's contract — what was bought, key SLAs, renewal timing — well enough to recognize when an operational issue has client implications and flag it immediately.
* Support clean handoffs to Sales when expansion opportunities are identified — nothing falls in the seam.

**Data & Reporting Discipline**

* Keep health scoring, CRM records, and success plans accurate, complete, and current — audit-ready at all times.
* Contribute to consolidated reporting that gives leadership a trusted single source of truth.
* Flag data gaps or health score discrepancies proactively — don't let a reporting issue become a surprise.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* 5+ years in health plan operations or an adjacent healthcare role. Direct customer-facing experience — account management, implementation support, or customer service — with at least one example of owning an issue end to end.
* Foundational literacy across payer operations — follows an operational conversation in any domain and knows where to go for depth. Basic regulatory and plan-finance awareness, with working knowledge expected within 12–18 months.
* Knows the basics of assigned accounts' contracts — what was bought, key SLAs, renewal timing — well enough to recognize when an operational issue has commercial implications and flags it. Building toward commercial fluency; never negotiates, always escalates commercial questions framed.
* Operates inside a recovery with full ownership of assigned pieces: keeps the issue list current and honest, tracks every action to closure, preps status materials, and never lets recovery items die in a seam. Learns escalation mechanics by running the machinery of one.
* Demonstrated workstream management — has personally run a plan with named owners, dates, and dependencies through to completion, including tracking actions to closure and keeping stakeholders current without being asked. Formal methodology or certification (PMP, agile/scrum) a plus, not required.
* Exposure to payer claims, pricing, or medical-management platforms (e.g., Facets, QNXT, HealthRules Payer, or comparable systems). Comfortable with communication and project-management tools; willing adopter of AI tools (e.g., Claude). Knows which technical roles exist and when to pull them in.

**Preferred (Not Required)**

* Hands-on exposure to a system implementation, platform migration, or major upgrade from any seat — testing, data conversion, cutover support, training, or PMO. Has lived the rhythm of a go-live. Experience on the health-plan side of a vendor relationship — having been the customer is a differentiator. HealthEdge product suite familiarity.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**

**In the First 90 Days**

* Has reviewed and understands the success plan for every assigned account — knows the outcome, the current health score, and the open workstreams.
* Owns at least one defined workstream per assigned account and is keeping it current, honest, and moving without being asked.
* Has built working relationships with key internal counterpart

new_jobs.title: Senior Sales Compensation Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.

We're remote-first by design and operate with intelligence at the center of everything we do. At Block, you'll be challenged by some of the brightest, most creative minds in the industry and have the tools and autonomy to do the most meaningful work of your career.

#### **The Role**

We're looking for a Senior Sales Compensation Operations Analyst to independently lead complex commissions administration across multiple plans and sales populations. You'll own end-to-end commission cycles, resolve complex operational issues, and strengthen the controls and processes behind accurate, timely payments.

As a senior individual contributor, you'll partner with Finance, Payroll, Sales Operations, HR, and technical teams to drive improvements, support approved plan changes, and develop the team's operational expertise. This role owns the administration of approved sales compensation plans, not sales compensation plan design.

#### **You Will**

* Independently own end-to-end commission cycles across multiple plans and sales populations, managing timelines, dependencies, approvals, and validated payment submissions to Payroll.
* Interpret and apply approved plan rules for participant eligibility, quotas, sales crediting, effective dates, and adjustments; oversee accurate plan assignments and participant changes.
* Own complex reconciliations across sales transactions, commission calculations, adjustments, and payment totals, resolving discrepancies before payment submission.
* Serve as an escalation point for complex commission inquiries, explain calculations and outcomes clearly, and coordinate resolution within approved policies. Document exceptions and secure required approvals.
* Design and strengthen operational controls, review procedures, and audit documentation to improve accuracy, consistency, and traceability.
* Lead root-cause analysis of recurring issues and use operational reporting to prioritize improvements that reduce errors, manual work, and payment risk.
* Lead operational readiness and user acceptance testing for approved plan, process, and system changes, partnering with technical teams to define requirements, validate results, and resolve issues.
* Mentor teammates, guide complex cases, and improve shared procedures and training materials to strengthen team capability and consistency.

#### **You Have**

* 5+ years of experience in sales compensation, commissions administration, or related operations.
* Demonstrated experience in sales commissions administration, including independent ownership of complex payment cycles across multiple plans or sales populations.
* Strong spreadsheet and analytical skills, including advanced formulas, lookups, pivot tables, and reconciliation of large datasets.
* Ability to interpret complex compensation plan rules, investigate discrepancies, and distinguish routine administration decisions from exceptions requiring approval.
* Experience developing operational controls, supporting audits, and leading process improvements through implementation.
* Experience translating business requirements into test scenarios, validating results, and assessing readiness for plan, process, or system changes.
* Strong cross-functional communication and influencing skills, including explaining sensitive payment issues and resolving competing priorities.
* Sound judgment, discretion with confidential compensation information, and the ability to manage ambiguity while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.

#### **Nice to Have**

* Experience administering incentive compensation platforms, such as Pigment, Xactly, CaptivateIQ, or Spiff.
* SQL skills for querying, validating, and analyzing commission-related data.

#### **Technologies We Use and Teach**

* Pigment for ICM/quota issuance, Salesforce as the system of record & end user UI in Looker.
